title: Extramammary Paget Disease, Vulvar Melanoma & Rare Vulvar Tumors: Immunohistochemistry, Breslow Depth and KIT Mutations

steps.say: Extramammary Paget disease of the vulva is a rare intraepithelial adenocarcinoma presenting with chronic pruritus and a pathognomonic macroscopic appearance.
steps.tx: Vulvar **extramammary Paget disease (EMPD)** classically presents as an erythematous, eczematoid, velvety plaque studded with white islands of hyperkeratosis, described pathognomonically as a **strawberries and cream plaque**. Histologically, intraepidermal **Paget cells** display abundant **pale cytoplasm** and atypical vesicular nuclei. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

steps.say: Immunohistochemical staining is essential to distinguish primary cutaneotrophic Paget disease from secondary epidermotropic spread of internal adenocarcinomas.
steps.tx: In **primary EMPD IHC**, cells are characteristically **CK7 positive CK20 negative** and GCDFP-15 positive, confirming apocrine/sweat gland origin. Conversely, **secondary EMPD CK20 positive CDX2 positive** points to underlying urothelial or **colorectal primary** adenocarcinoma secondarily spreading into the perineal epidermis. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

steps.say: All patients diagnosed with extramammary Paget disease must undergo systematic screening to exclude occult invasive carcinoma or synchronistic internal malignancies.
steps.tx: Clinical evaluation must investigate for an **underlying invasive adenocarcinoma 10-15%** arising within the dermis, as well as an **associated internal malignancy 20-30%** (colorectal, urothelial, or breast carcinoma), mandating comprehensive **systemic screening** with colonoscopy, mammography, and pelvic imaging. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Perform full-thickness vulvar punch biopsy confirming intraepidermal Paget cells
Perform IHC panel: CK7, CK20, CDX2, GATA3, and GCDFP-15
Conduct screening: colonoscopy, cystoscopy, mammography, and pelvic CT
Plan definitive wide local excision or topical immunomodulatory therapy

steps.say: Surgical management of extramammary Paget disease is challenging because subclinical microscopic extension frequently extends far beyond visible lesion borders.
steps.tx: Because intraepidermal disease demonstrates irregular **skip lesions**, surgical excision carries a high local **recurrence rate 30-40%**. For widespread, multifocal, or recurrent non-invasive lesions, medical therapy using **topical imiquimod 5%** cream or **photodynamic therapy** achieves excellent tissue-sparing disease control. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Surgical Wide Local Excision
points: Resection with 1 to 2 cm gross margins and frozen sections
High rate of microscopically positive margins (due to skip lesions)
Risk of substantial vulvar scarring and architectural distortion

right.title: Topical Imiquimod 5% Cream
points: Toll-like receptor 7 agonist stimulating local interferon release
Applied 3 times weekly for 12 to 16 weeks
Complete clinical and histological response rates exceeding 70%

steps.say: Vulvar melanoma is the second most common vulvar malignancy, arising predominantly on non-hair-bearing mucosal surfaces of the clitoris and labia minora.
steps.tx: Malignant **vulvar melanoma** represents the **second most common vulvar cancer** (accounting for 5% of vulvar malignancies). The tumor occurs predominantly in postmenopausal women with a characteristic **clitoral/labia minora location** and is staged pathologically by microscopic **Breslow depth** of invasion. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

steps.say: Surgical resection margins for vulvar melanoma are determined strictly by Breslow microstaging thickness rather than macroscopic lesion diameter.
steps.tx: Current surgical **Breslow margins** require a clear surgical **margin 1 cm for <=1 mm** thickness and a **margin 2 cm for >2 mm** depth of invasion. Deep subcutaneous tissue is resected to the muscular fascia, avoiding unnecessary ultraradical vulvectomies that do not improve survival.

nodes.label: Perform complete excisional biopsy of suspicious pigmented vulvar lesion
Determine exact Breslow depth of invasion and presence of ulceration
Execute wide local excision with 1 cm or 2 cm margin based on thickness
Perform sentinel lymph node biopsy for tumors > 0.8 to 1.0 mm thickness

steps.say: Mucosal melanomas of the vulva exhibit a unique genomic driver mutation profile distinct from cutaneous sun-exposed melanomas.
steps.tx: Vulvar melanomas harbor frequent oncogenic **KIT mutations 15-25%** localized to **exons 11 and 13**, conferring clinical **imatinib sensitivity** in advanced metastatic disease, while demonstrating a characteristically **low BRAF mutation <10%** frequency compared to cutaneous melanomas. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Vulvar Mucosal Melanoma Genetics
points: Responsive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (imatinib, nilotinib)
Low frequency of BRAF V600E mutations (<10%)

right.title: Cutaneous Cutaneous Melanoma Genetics
points: High frequency of BRAF V600E mutations (50% to 60%)
Responsive to combined BRAF and MEK inhibitors (dabrafenib/trametinib)

steps.say: Carcinoma of the Bartholin gland represents a rare vulvar malignancy characterized by deep posterior labial location and specific diagnostic criteria.
steps.tx: Diagnosis of **Bartholin gland carcinoma** requires fulfillment of the classic **Honan criteria** (correct anatomical location, histology compatible with gland origin, and absence of another primary tumor). Adenoid cystic carcinoma variants characteristically exhibit **adenoid cystic perineural invasion** and recurrent **MYB-NFIB fusion**.
